# `₁` `₋₁` — Subscripts

A subscript is postfix. It selects a major cell of the array just before it, with no space between them, so `v₁` is `1⌷v`. A negative subscript counts from the end. Type a subscript digit with Alt-5 then the digit, and a negative one with Alt-5 then `-` then the digit.

```bpl
v←10 20 30
v₁                 ⍝ 20
v₋₁                ⍝ 30
[1 2 ⋄ 3 4]₁       ⍝ 3 4
```

An item with a subscript can be an assignment target. A subscript binds as tightly as a superscript, so `v₁²` squares the selected item.

```bpl
v←10 20 30
v₁←5 ⋄ v           ⍝ 10 5 30
v₁+←1 ⋄ v          ⍝ 10 6 30
v₁²                ⍝ 36
```

A subscript writes one literal position on the leading axis. Use [`⌷`](squad.qmd) for a computed position, several positions, a key or another axis.

## Errors

- `SYNTAX`: a space between the item and its subscript, or `₋` with no digit after it
- `INDEX`: the position is outside the leading axis
- `LENGTH`: the item is a unit, which has no axis to select from
